title: Sin Nature
definition: Sin nature describes the corrupted condition of fallen humanity that inclines people away from God and toward sin.
summary: Humanity is not merely weak but deeply corrupted by sin and in need of grace.
christFocus: Jesus came as the sinless Savior to rescue people from sin's guilt, power, and final consequences.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The sin nature means that sin is not only something people do; it reflects a deeper corruption within fallen humanity. Human beings are responsible for sinful choices, yet those choices come from hearts affected by sin.

This doctrine does not deny human dignity, because people remain image-bearers. But it does deny that humanity can fix itself apart from God's grace.

The Gospel answers the sin nature through Christ. He forgives guilt, gives new life, breaks sin's dominion, and begins the work of renewal by the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often underestimate sin by treating it as mistakes, wounds, or bad habits only. Sin nature matters because it shows why people need more than advice, willpower, or self-improvement; they need redemption.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop minimizing sin or trusting self-reform as ultimate. Bring your heart to God honestly, trust Christ for forgiveness, and depend on the Spirit for new obedience.
